name: Bani
overview: Bani is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra, identified specifically as a descendant who had married a foreign wife. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. The mention of Bani highlights issues related to intermarriage during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Bani means "descendant" in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given by God but serves as a straightforward personal identifier in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Bani as a descendant, emphasizing his genealogical line, but does not provide further family relationships beyond the note of his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Bani is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of the post-exilic community's challenges in maintaining purity of worship and covenant identity. The mention of his foreign wife in Ezra 10:38 underscores the community's efforts to address intermarriage with non-Israelite peoples, which was seen as a threat to their covenant faithfulness. Thus, Bani's record serves to illustrate the broader call to holiness and separation in the restored Israel.
